fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From Skeptic to Gematrinator", "body": "Derek says his awakening came in two waves: a coworker showing him a 9/11 video in 2004, then coverage of the 2015 Charleston church shooting that felt built to make him feel something rather than report the facts. Tired of slickly produced truther channels, he found Zachary Hubbard's plain screen shares of basic numerology, ran the ciphers in Excel and eventually built gematrinator.com. He calls the 2016 World Series his turning point, when he told coworkers the Cubs would fall behind three games to one, then win in seven and in extra innings, and he credits Hubbard sharing his first video with making him known in the community almost overnight."}, {"title": "Is Truth Seeking a Spiritual Practice?", "body": "Chance asks whether conspiracy research, when it is authentic and really about finding the truth, is a form of spiritual work, adding that he now judges controlled opposition by how hard it tries to scare you. Derek answers that the matrix people talk about escaping is a matrix of control, a spiritual system humans take part in but which he believes is inspired by dark energies, whether called Satan or the demiurge. He leans on natural law and Mark Passio's long seminar on it, which Chance also recommends, and says a strong spiritual experience at sixteen left him hoping God will protect him as long as he is helping people."}, {"title": "Chance's Case That Darkness Cannot Create", "body": "Chance describes God, or the infinite, as something very like imagination, a free-flowing source of novelty that runs on its own the way dreams do, and argues that forces cut off from source cannot imagine or create, only scavenge, which he suggests is why a slave grid suits them better than mass extermination. Derek builds on it with music, contending that big radio hits are engineered scientifically rather than creatively, while the uplifting trance heard at festivals that sell out in minutes never reaches FM radio. He extends the pattern to mainstream comedians and scripted wrestling promos, arguing the system has to manipulate creative people and twist their message."}, {"title": "Base Ciphers and the Kobe Decode", "body": "With the gematrinator.com calculator on screen share, Derek walks through his base ciphers: English ordinal, which numbers the alphabet one through 26, a reduction that collapses each letter to a single digit, the reversed orders, Jewish or Latin gematria, and English Extended, modelled on Hebrew and Greek letter values. Along the way he argues that the name Kobe sums to 33, a number he says marks basketball legends and the crucifixion code, and that Kobe Bryant's age at death, 41 years and 157 days, matches his name's values. Chance offers that anyone hiding a message in plain sight would use several ciphers rather than one, and Derek agrees."}, {"title": "Sun, Moon and a Plane at Totality", "body": "Derek argues that 666 is misunderstood and really describes the geometry of the Earth, Sun and Moon, citing an axis he puts at 66.6 degrees from the plane to the Sun and a Moon diameter of 2,160 miles, and he ties the code to eclipses, including a total solar eclipse on the summer solstice in 2001. Chance recalls watching the 2017 eclipse at a small festival in Missouri, where he and one other person without eclipse glasses saw a plane cross the returning sun trailing pink clouds that nobody else he talked to noticed. Derek, who watched from Southern Illinois, calls the returning light one of the most powerful parts."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Derek Tikkuri joins us for a math-magical show to decode the spells of language and mass-media manipulations. Better known as Gematrinator, Derek reveals numerical riddles and teaches the trippy coincidences that multiply once one begins using letter/number ciphers (Gematria) to analyze names, dates, headlines, and all the words that make up our world.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Finishing the 666 Riddle", "body": "Back for the members' hour with the screen share running again, Derek resumes the 666 riddle he ties to the coronavirus, starting from the simplest layer: corona is a six-letter word, Revelation is the sixty-sixth book of the Bible, and his English Sumerian cipher is just the alphabet multiplied by six, echoing the sixty minutes and sixty seconds we count time by. Chance admits the prime-number steps outpace him and calls the whole practice like learning a new language, and Derek freely credits a find to his Discord community, where researchers trade decodes all day."}, {"title": "Where the Organic Code Ends", "body": "Chance asks the question that had been on his mind a lot lately: can anyone really draw a line between contrived events and the numbers woven into ordinary life? Derek answers that gematria on YouTube is barely six years old, that he has taken flak for backing off from calling everything a conspiracy, and that without an insider stepping forward it could still simply be a function of reality. Chance describes how festivals and a few key psychedelic experiences showed him the unity of all things, and Derek frames gematria as mysticism, with guidelines and observed methods but no hard rules."}, {"title": "Speaking the World into Existence", "body": "Derek grounds his theory in Genesis: if God spoke the world into being and made man in his image, then people may be creating the world with their own words. He walks through the Kabbalah's Tree of Life, where thought filters down to Malkuth, the manifested sphere, and contrasts Yahweh as infinite possibility with Elohim as manifested reality. His stories follow, from a man at Anarchadelphia who always loved 47 and whose name, John, sums to it, to a sister-in-law whose lucky 13 runs through her life. Chance adds that the unconscious already knows this code, which is how spellcraft works."}, {"title": "A Life Written in Numbers", "body": "Derek lays out the synchronicities that convinced him the code is organic: his own name matching the word gematria, a house bought for exactly $130,000 and moved into on his thirty-second birthday, and a childhood habit of telling people he was 43, the value of Derek. He points to the films The Number 23 and Pi, whose lead actor shares his June 4 birthday. Chance pushes back on reading this as a simulation, arguing the internal consistency suggests a very real world with a playful intelligence behind it, and raises 26 as both God and game, prompting Derek's note on the body's 206 bones."}, {"title": "Rituals, Government and the Eclipse X", "body": "Derek explains why he believes staged events follow the numbers: mirroring the natural code avoids setting off subconscious alarms, and the clues left behind force a choice to look away, which under natural law counts as consent. He links transportation tragedies to Mercury, ruler of Gemini and Libra, and breaks government down from gubernare into steering the mind. Chance answers that truth is the only real authority and connects police and polarity to a charge generated by division. Derek then maps two eclipses crossing America in an X, notes headlines and published measurements quietly changing, and calls flat Earth a distraction."}]
